messages:
jen: Hi team, first day! trying to get the monorepo running. I'm stuck connecting to Postgres started via docker-compose. The db service shows healthy but my app keeps timing out with `could not connect to server: Connection refused`. Any hints?

rui: welcome Jen! quick sanity check: are you running the app inside a container or on host? if inside container, host=localhost is wrong.

jen: running the app locally (node) on my laptop, not in a container. docker-compose has a `ports: - "5432:5432"` mapping. ENV is `DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pass@localhost:5432/devdb`.

alex: ok since app is on host, localhost should work. do `docker-compose ps` and `docker-compose logs db`. also `pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432` from host to try.

jen: `pg_isready -h localhost` fails: "could not connect to server: Connection refused". `docker-compose logs db` shows `could not change ownership of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Operation not permitted` and Postgres exits.

rui: that's a permission error on the mounted host volume. on macs (esp M1/M2) the container user (999) may not be able to chown the host folder. two options: 1) chown the host directory to 999:999 (`sudo chown -R 999:999 ./data/db`) or 2) use a named volume instead of a host bind (remove the host path and use `- db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data` in compose).

jen: tried chown and restarted, now logs say Postgres ready but app still times out. `ps aux | grep postgres` on host shows nothing (expected), `docker-compose exec db pg_isready -U postgres` returns `accepting connections`.

alex: if the container reports ready and host pg_isready fails, maybe Docker Desktop is binding to a different interface. Try `telnet localhost 5432` or `nc -vz localhost 5432`. Also check `docker ps` to confirm port published.

jen: `docker ps` shows `0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp` for the db container. `nc -vz localhost 5432` times out. weird.

rui: sometimes macOS firewall or another local process conflicts. Do `lsof -i :5432` on host to see if something else is binding. Also try `docker-compose down` then `docker-compose up --force-recreate` to ensure the port mapping is applied.

jen: `lsof -i :5432` returns nothing. Recreate didn't help. I see this in docker logs: `could not create lock file /var/lib/postgresql/data/postmaster.pid: Permission denied` even after chown.

alex: hmm. are you using "bind mounts" to a directory inside iCloud/Dropbox or a path that has special permissions? Try moving the data dir to a plain folder under your home like `~/redwood-scratch/db` and chown that. Also check Docker Desktop file sharing preferences for that path.

jen: moved folder, chowned to 999:999, cleaned volumes with `docker-compose down -v` and now host `pg_isready -h localhost` succeeds. App can connect. thanks!

infra-bot: note: If you're on Apple Silicon and the postgres image lacks arm64 support, add `platform: linux/amd64` under the service or pick an arm64-compatible image. See internal note: /handbook/dev/local-db.

devex-bot: pinned by devex: short checklist for local DBs: 1) host vs container hostname 2) volume ownership (UID 999) 3) avoid cloud-synced paths 4) named volumes for easiest setup 5) tcp sockets inside containers (no unix sockets across containers). Link: https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-quickstart

jen: huge help everyone — got it working and documented the exact commands in my onboarding notes. one small question: if I add Redis later, should I expose ports?

rui: for local dev you can expose redis port, but if your app runs in compose too, prefer using service name `redis:6379` inside containers and avoid exposing unless you need host clients. Also remember redis clients sometimes try unix sockets by default on mac; force TCP with `redis://redis:6379/0`.

jen: noted. thanks again :)
